teacherNotes.title: Core Words
teacherNotes.content: rent, landlord, tenant, housewarming, party, invite, visit, new, home, welcome, address

elements.content: Core Active Vocabulary (10-20 items):
rent, landlord, tenant, housewarming, party, invite, visit, new, home, welcome, address
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I want to rent a two-room flat (stating rental request)
• Come to my housewarming party on Sunday! (extending invitation)
• What is your new address? (asking contact info)
• Welcome to my new home! (welcoming guests)
Pronunciation Focus:
Pronunciation of /aɪ/ in 'invite' and /eə/ in 'flatshare/tenancy'.

teacherNotes.title: Grammar Function
teacherNotes.content: Imperatives & Invitation Structures ('Come to my housewarming!', 'Would you like to visit my new flat?')

elements.content: Grammar System & Functional Framing:
Imperatives & Invitation Structures ('Come to my housewarming!', 'Would you like to visit my new flat?')
Controlled Practice:
You moved to a new flat and want to invite a friend over. What do you say?
options: Come to my housewarming party on Sunday!
answers: Come to my housewarming party on Sunday!

elements.content: Reading Script & Dialogue:

A: I moved to a new apartment last week!
B: Congratulations! Are you having a housewarming party?
A: Yes! Would you like to come this Sunday at six?
B: I'd love to! Please send me your new address.
Listening Comprehension:
Listen to a voice message inviting a friend to a housewarming party and note the date, time, and address.
